# Behavioral Specification — Userinfo Handling (`/workspace/dataset/test2_executable`)

## Distilled rules

**R1 — Userinfo survives `set(host=...)` verbatim.** Only the host component is replaced; username, password, port, path, and their existing encoding are untouched.
- `--a 'http://user:pass@example.com/p' --b 'newhost.com'` → stdout `http://user:pass@newhost.com/p`, exit 0
- `--a 'http://user@example.com/p' --b 'newhost.com'` → `http://user@newhost.com/p`, exit 0
- Port preserved: `--a 'http://user:pass@example.com:8080/p'` → `http://user:pass@newhost.com:8080/p`, exit 0
- Userinfo case preserved while host is lowercased: `--a 'http://USER:PASS@EXAMPLE.COM/p' --b 'NEWHOST.COM'` → `http://USER:PASS@newhost.com/p`

**R2 — Degenerate userinfo is kept as-is.** `user:@`, `:pass@`, and even bare `@` all pass through unchanged:
- `--a 'http://user:@example.com/p'` → `http://user:@newhost.com/p`
- `--a 'http://:pass@example.com/p'` → `http://:pass@newhost.com/p`
- `--a 'http://@example.com/p'` → `http://@newhost.com/p`

**R3 — Extra `:` inside the password is tolerated but percent-encoded on output** (first `:` splits user/pass; the rest are encoded):
- `--a 'http://user:p:a:ss@example.com/p'` → `http://user:p%3Aa%3Ass@newhost.com/p`, exit 0
- `--a 'http://user::pass@example.com/p'` → `http://user:%3Apass@newhost.com/p`, exit 0

**R4 — Raw `@` inside userinfo is fatal at parse time.** Splitting happens at the *last* `@`, so everything after it is treated as the host and fails host validation. Crash occurs in `furl(args.a)` (line 9 of the embedded script), exit 1, nothing on stdout; stderr ends with:
```
ValueError: Invalid host 'ss@example.com'. Host strings must have at least one non-period character, can't contain any of '!@#$%^&'"*()+=:;/', and can't have adjacent periods.
[PYI-949:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test2' due to unhandled exception!
```
(`--a 'http://user:p@ss@example.com/p'` → host parsed as `ss@example.com`; `--a 'http://us@er@example.com/p'` → host parsed as `er@example.com`.)

**R5 — Percent-encoded userinfo passes through unchanged** (no double-encoding, no decoding): `--a 'http://user:p%40ss@example.com/p'` → `http://user:p%40ss@newhost.com/p`; `--a 'http://user%40name:pa%3Ass@example.com/p'` → `http://user%40name:pa%3Ass@newhost.com/p`.

**R6 — `set(host=...)` treats `--b` as a pure, literal host string — it is never parsed** for userinfo/port/path. Any of `!@#$%^&'"*()+=:;/` (or `?`, `#`, `&`) in `--b` raises ValueError at the `f.set(host=args.b)` call (line 10), exit 1, empty stdout:

- `--b 'h.com:99'` → `ValueError: Invalid host 'h.com:99'. ...` (port cannot be smuggled via host)
- `--b 'a/b'` → `ValueError: Invalid host 'a/b'. ...`
- `--b 'user%40h.com'` → rejected too (`%` is in the forbidden set)
- `--b 'h?x#y&z'` → rejected
- Also rejected: all-period hosts (`--b '...'`) and adjacent periods (`--b 'a..b'`), same message.

**R7 — Lenient host cases:**
- `--b ''` (empty) is accepted and removes the host: → `http:///p`, exit 0
- Spaces are *not* rejected: `--b 'NEW Host.com'` → `http://new host.com/p` (lowercased, space kept)
- IPv6 literal passes: `--b '[::1]'` → `http://[::1]/p` (brackets/colons inside an IPv6 literal are fine)
- Unicode host is punycode-encoded: `--b 'münchen.de'` → `http://xn--mnchen-3ya.de/p`
- Trailing dot kept: `--b 'host.'` → `http://host./p`

- **Success:** single line on stdout (the URL), empty stderr, exit 0.

1. **`set(host='')` clears the host to empty, but the `//` separator always remains.** Scheme-less URLs render as `//<rest>`; schemed URLs as `<scheme>://<rest>` (e.g. `http://`, `http:///path?q=1#f`). Host is gone; the authority marker is not.
2. **`--a` whitespace handling is asymmetric**: whitespace-*only* `--a` values (space, tab, newline) behave identically to `''`. 3. **`--b` is never validated, stripped, or encoded.** Spaces, leading/trailing whitespace, and even embedded newlines are inserted verbatim into the host slot (`http://ho st.com`, `http:// h.com `, literal newline in output).
4. **Degenerate-but-parseable `--a` components survive host replacement**: path-only, query-only, fragment-only inputs become `//<b><component>`; with `--b ''` they become `//` + component (e.g. `///path/only`, `//?q=1`, `//#frag`).
5. **Empty original host with port/userinfo**: `http://user@:8080/` parses with an empty host; setting a new host fills the slot cleanly (`http://user@h.com:8080/`), and `set(host='')` is a no-op (output identical to input).
6. **Trailing slash on `--a` is preserved** through the host swap (`http://h.com/` vs `http://h.com`); with `--b ''` it yields `http:///`.
7. **Path spaces are percent-encoded** (`/a b` → `/a%20b`) — encoding applies to path components only, never to `--b`.

# Behavioral spec: path/query/fragment preservation & encoding

All probes exit `0` with empty stderr — every input in this category is accepted and normalized silently. All outputs are `--b` host-substituted (`h` → `n`), stdout is a single line.

## Distilled rules

**General pipeline:** URL is fully decoded then re-encoded on output (not verbatim passthrough). Hex digits of surviving `%XX` sequences are **uppercased**.

**Path:**
- Valid percent-encodings of *unreserved* chars are decoded to the literal char: `/%41%42` → `/AB`, `/%7Euser` → `/~user`.
- Valid encodings of *reserved* chars are preserved (hex uppercased): `/a%2fb%2Fc` → `/a%2Fb%2Fc`, `/p%23x` → `/p%23x`, `/a%3Fb` → `/a%3Fb`, `/%00` → `/%00`.

- **Invalid `%` sequences get the bare `%` re-encoded as `%25`:** `/a%zz` → `/a%25zz`, `/100%` → `/100%25`, `/%` → `/%25`, `/%2` → `/%252`.

- `\t`, `\r`, `\n` are **stripped** (browser-style): `/a\tb` and `/a\r\nb` → `/ab`.
- **No dot-segment or slash normalization:** `/a/./b/../c`, `//a//b`, `///` all preserved verbatim.

**Query:**
- Space → `+` (form-encoding): `?q=a b` → `?q=a+b`; pre-encoded key `%20` also normalizes to `+` (`?a%20b=c` → `?a+b=c`).

**Fragment:**
- Preserved with same re-encoding rules: `#f g` → `#f%20g`, `#fé` → `#f%C3%A9`, `#f%2fg` → `#f%2Fg`, second `#` → `%23` (`#f#g` → `#f%23g`); `/`, `?`, `;~+` pass through verbatim (`#a/b?c=d`, `#;~+` unchanged).

- In the **path** `\` is encoded: `/p\q` → `/p%5Cq`.

--a 'http://h/%41%42'     --b n → http://n/AB
--a 'http://h/a%2fb%2Fc'  --b n → http://n/a%2Fb%2Fc
